source.title: A PAC-Bayesian Link Between Generalisation and Flat Minima
source.authors: Maxime Haddouche; Paul Viallard; Umut Simsekli; Benjamin Guedj

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper develops theoretical links between gradient-based flatness and generalisation, and reports a neural-network empirical assessment. Its experiment does not measure the train–test gap or the magnitude-aware perturbation measure specified in any claim version.
record.gate_note: The empirical section reports QSB constants and test risks for two datasets. No results directly test the exact behaviours or measures in V1–V8; the reported findings are recorded under fits_no_version. Figure values are not numerically recoverable from the text.
record.test_reason: The study derives bounds involving gradient norms and assesses a QSB condition. Neither its theory nor its experiments test V7's magnitude-aware perturbation measure or its ranking of generalization gaps. It reports no comparisons testing V1–V6 or V8.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors derive conditional links between flatness and generalization, including transitory 1/m rates when empirical error and expected gradients are small. Their experiment supports the QSB assumption for the tested small CNN posteriors; it does not directly verify a sharpness–generalization correlation. How optimization attains flat minima remains open.
record.recipe_differences: The paper derives PAC-Bayesian bounds using Poincaré and log-Sobolev inequalities and gradients, rather than directly testing the interventions or measures in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The empirical assessment uses MNIST and FashionMNIST; the authors report different relationships between training-loss and 0-1 test-risk performance across the two datasets.

fits_no_version.finding: Estimated QSB constants decrease from approximately 0.55 to 0.45 on both datasets. Bounded-cross-entropy and 0–1 test-risk performance nearly match on MNIST but differ on FashionMNIST.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For the tested Gaussian posteriors around a small CNN, the estimated QSB constant remains below one during SGD training on MNIST and FashionMNIST; surrogate-loss and classification-risk behavior depends on the dataset.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorems provide generalization bounds involving gradient norms under Poincare, QSB, or log-Sobolev assumptions, with additional complexity terms. These are sufficient bounds rather than empirical rankings of magnitude-aware sharpness.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under specified distributional and loss assumptions, low empirical risk and small expected gradient norms can yield small PAC-Bayesian risk bounds when the remaining complexity terms are controlled.

record.code_released: not stated; the text says source code is available at a link but supplies no URL.
record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Algorithmic Learning Theory; Proceedings of Machine Learning Research, vol. 272, 2025.
record.problems: The empirical assessment covers two datasets and one small CNN architecture. Figure 1 values are plotted but not tabulated; the text gives only approximate C values and qualitative comparisons. The empirical section assesses the QSB assumption, not a train–test gap or the magnitude-aware sharpness measure.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label generalization, and chance-level random-label held-out accuracy.
Width-dependent test error beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and local-connectivity effects.
Adaptive versus SGD performance under different tuning regimes.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout effects and interactions with training-set size, augmentation, and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its association with measured train–test gaps, and ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Accuracy effects of removing memorized versus random training examples.

record.verdict_notes: References to counterexamples for flatness and to Jiang et al. are cited findings, not this study's results. No version-specific verdict is warranted.

versions.untested_parts: Width sweep past interpolation and test-error trend.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Large-batch comparisons under fixed epoch budgets.
Dropout comparisons and interactions with data augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance and its ranking of train–test gaps.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.
